rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient to observe all 10 compounds and locate the elution window and critical pairs. The moderate gradient duration and temperature provide a useful baseline for subsequent slope and temperature comparisons.

Lengthen only the gradient to determine whether the critical R = 0.82 pair responds to a shallower slope. This should improve separation while keeping the last peak near the 10-minute scoring threshold.

Raise the starting organic fraction to remove low-organic time and bring the last peak below 10 minutes. The slightly shallower gradient should preserve or improve the now-resolved critical pair, while the scouting run suggests enough retention remains for the early peaks.

Injection 3 already achieves the maximum CRF; retain it as the benchmark. Raise temperature by one step to seek a shorter fully resolved separation while checking temperature selectivity at the critical pair.

Return to the temperature of the maximum-score method and raise phi0 one step to shorten retention. The narrower gradient window may preserve the critical separation; monitor both that pair and the increasingly compressed early peaks.

Test a higher temperature beyond the apparent critical-pair convergence, where an elution-order reversal may restore resolution. Shorten the gradient to seek a substantially faster separation, retaining injection 3 as the maximum-score fallback.

Increase only temperature to map the new critical pair’s selectivity near 55 C. This tests whether passing through its apparent convergence restores full resolution while further shortening the 6.85-minute separation.

Lengthen only the gradient to test the slope response of the high-temperature critical pair. There is ample time margin below 10 minutes, so a shallower gradient could recover full resolution with a faster separation than injection 3.

The high-temperature critical pair worsened when the gradient was lengthened, so test a substantially steeper gradient instead. This may improve its selectivity while shortening the separation; check whether other pairs become limiting.

Explore lower-temperature selectivity with a shorter gradient than the fully resolved benchmark. Cooling may separate the central cluster after an order reversal, while the 12-minute gradient should keep the last peak below 10 minutes.

Test an intermediate temperature with a steeper gradient to shift selectivity away from the close pairs seen at 45 and 55–60 C. This explores a much faster separation while retaining injection 3 as the proven maximum-CRF method.

Lower the starting organic fraction to test window-dependent selectivity for the critical pair at 55 C. Comparing with injection 6 will show whether this restores resolution while retaining a substantial time advantage over injection 3.
Shorten the fastest fully resolved method by one gradient-time step to test its resolution boundary. Injection 12 remains the maximum-score fallback if either marginal pair drops below R = 1.5.

Trim the gradient window to reduce initial retention while making the slope shallower than injection 12. This balances the starting-composition and slope effects on the critical pairs, seeking full resolution with a slightly earlier last peak.

Lower phi1 one step from injection 14 to make the gradient slightly shallower and lift its R = 1.47 critical pair above threshold. The last peak should remain comfortably below 10 minutes, potentially providing another maximum-score method.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a much faster gradient on the opposite side of the central pair’s selectivity crossover. The low starting organic fraction should retain the early peaks, while this run checks whether full resolution is possible in a substantially shorter separation.

Refine the near-optimal injection 5 by lowering phi1 one step, making the gradient shallower to improve its R = 1.35 critical pair. Its 9.02-minute last peak leaves some time margin to recover full resolution without a time penalty.

Test whether a higher starting organic fraction shifts the high-temperature critical pair farther apart while shortening retention. Monitor the first pair closely, since early-peak compression may limit this faster alternative; injection 12 remains the fastest proven fully resolved method.

Seek more resolution margin than the marginally resolved 55 C methods by combining a higher starting fraction with a shallower gradient. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, potentially yielding maximum CRF with better separation of both critical pairs.

Lower phi1 one step from injection 19 to improve its sole unresolved pair through a slightly shallower gradient. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, with a chance of greater critical-pair resolution margin than the existing maximum-score methods.

Trim injection 12’s unused high-organic gradient segment while preserving its starting composition, temperature, and exact slope. Its last peak eluted near organic fraction 0.57, so ending at 0.65 should preserve maximum CRF with a shorter programmed gradient.

Test a modest slope increase from 0.075 to 0.080 organic fraction per minute, between the fully resolved injection 12 and the steeper unresolved injection 13. This seeks a shorter separation while locating the critical pair’s resolution boundary more precisely.

Slightly flatten injection 20’s gradient to seek more resolution margin while keeping the last peak below 10 minutes. Injection 12 remains the fastest fully resolved benchmark; this run targets a less marginal maximum-score alternative.

Use a slope between injections 14 and 15 to seek full resolution with a shorter separation than injection 15. The proposed slope of 0.065 organic fraction per minute should bring the marginal pair just above R = 1.5 while keeping the last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.

Interpolate the slopes of fully resolved injections 20 and 23 to target balanced critical-pair resolutions near 1.7 with the last peak below 10 minutes. Trim the unused high-organic segment to keep the programmed gradient short; injection 21 remains the fastest proven maximum-CRF method.
